Free cash flow stood at negative EUR 30.1 million. [#26](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-26)
Let me spend a moment on the macro backdrop, which remained difficult across Europe in the first half. [#59](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-59)
France posting record high insolvencies, Germany, its highest level of Q2 corporate insolvency since 2005 to name just two examples. [#60](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-60)
On costs, we did see a material increase in gas and electricity spot prices since the beginning of the conflict of around plus 50%. [#73](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-73)

We did see some inflation on other commodities used by the group, fuel, paper and chemicals, representing a EUR 7 million impact on cost in H1. [#77](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-77)

Growth in Germany was still impacted by a selective commercial approach in the Healthcare segment, reflecting ongoing budget pressures on clients. [#103](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-103)

On profitability, the EBITDA margin came in at 32% in H1, down 30 basis points, reflecting the temporary dilutive effect from the numerous acquisition in the region as well as a significant increase in the minimum legal salary in Germany, which remains difficult to fully pass through. [#111](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-111)
Limited top line growth currently makes it difficult to benefit from operating leverage. [#121](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-121)

Reported revenue, however, was down minus 0.8%, reflecting the negative evolution of the British pound, which had a minus 2.4% impact on revenue. [#126](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-126)
Turning to Ireland, the picture was more challenging with increased competition in hospitality weighing on performance. [#130](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-130)

The EBITDA margin of the region came in at 31.8%, down 10 bps. The significant U.K. minimum wage increase remains difficult to fully pass through in a competitive environment. [#131](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-131)

As a result, 50% of the volume has been lost, representing around EUR 2 million per month since June or an expected EUR 14 million impact on full year 2026. [#139](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-139)

On the profitability side, the EBITDA margin declined by 180 bps to 30.8%, impacted by workforce cost increase in the region and by the volume losses in Mexico. [#146](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-146)

Labor cost inflation has been particularly strong since the start of the year with, for instance, a plus 23% minimum wage increase in Colombia and a plus 13% increase in Mexico, and this could not be fully passed through to pricing in H1, reflecting the typical lag between cost increase and pricing adjustments, an effect set to ease in H2. [#147](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-147)
The Mexico volume loss late in H1 temporarily lower capacity utilization. [#148](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-148)
It's a mix of more mature markets and tougher macro environments. [#206](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-206)

At group level, the margin stands flat at 34.7% with some headwind from inflation coming first from staff costs, with LatAm countries and Germany increasing strongly the cost [indiscernible] on the benefits and second from the Middle East crisis with fuel costs spreading to other commodities. [#208](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-208)
Depreciation represented EUR 483.8 million, resulting in adjusted EBIT of EUR 317 million, with the margin also flat at 15.1%. [#214](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-214)

The main items between EBIT and operating income are [indiscernible]operating income expenses, which amounted to minus EUR 12 million, slightly higher than last year. [#217](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-217)

Below operating income, net financial expense increased to EUR 73.9 million from EUR 64.9 million, reflecting higher average net debt related to the extraordinary 2026 share buyback program and the higher average interest cost following recent refinancings. [#226](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-226)
Change in working capital requirement was negative at EUR 164 million, against EUR 113 million last year. [#251](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-251)

All in, free cash flow came to negative EUR 30.1 million for the first half, slightly penalized by the seasonality of the CapEx on the working capital, but within the usual bandwidth of H1. [#262](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-262)
As a result, net financial debt stood at EUR 3,670 million at the end of June, compared to EUR 3,020 million at the end of '25. [#266](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-266)
Net financial leverage [indiscernible] have increased to 2.09 from 1.92 in June '25. [#276](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-276)

Looking at the impact on our share count on factoring in the soft call exercise in mid-October '26, we expect the average basic share count to decrease by 3.5% by year-end on the average fully-diluted share count to decrease by circa 5%. [#302](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-302)
Given you've lost some volume in Q2 in Mexico, but you're also implementing pricing adjustments to offset cost inflation. [#361](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-361)

And then secondly, on Mexico, the EUR 14 million impact that you expect for full year '26, does that assume that you don't win any of that volume back of that 50%? [#364](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-364)
At every moment, they can decide to stop with a small supplier because we know that they have a lot of trouble in quality of service. [#375](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-375)

So yes, it's possible, and we could recover some hospitals that are too much desperate from the low quality of service, but it's impossible for me to say that I'm sure, and it is not included in our forecast for the year '26. [#377](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-377)
Firstly, you've highlighted the normal seasonality in the cash flow, but there's also a deterioration in DSOs in the half. [#402](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-402)
So here, this plant is stopped because people are not able to reach the plant. [#440](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-440)

We lose some turnover, of course, because we have some customers that are closed now, but it is not so meaningful for the group because we estimate that we have probably a risk for this summer around 1 million, not more than that for this lack of volume in hospitality in this region. [#449](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-449)
It is the magnitude of what we could lose. [#450](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-450)
So for the full year, the Middle East extra cost due to fuel, chemical and so on, of course, it will depend on the length of the war. [#461](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-461)
And so we have a kind of uncertainty there. [#462](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-462)
But let's say that it could be EUR 20 million to EUR 25 million. [#464](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-464)

In '27, we will be much more stronger to start the year, thanks to the indexes that will sustain the price negotiation at the end of the year '26 because we see today all the indexes related, of course, to labor cost and wages, but also all the indexes related to the other component of our P&L, so energy, fuel, even textile and so on, everything is growing fast. [#471](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-471)

So I would say that I know that everything is under severe pressure and super worry about French election in '27 and so on, but it was the mess in '26 and so on. [#476](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-476)
When you see the mess, we have a budget and the super bad economic climate for all the small customer. [#477](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-477)
We know that this year, it is a record level of bankruptcy in the French economy. [#478](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-478)
So really, the country is in a bad shape even in '26. [#479](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-479)
So it's exactly the same problems that we had end of Q3 and beginning of Q4 quite a low level of signature of new contract. [#496](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-496)

You've obviously seen some margin pressure in the first half, and you've called out both the lost volumes as well as the labor cost characteristics there. [#517](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-517)
So for '27, so we are not in position, of course, to give any kind of precise guidance for '27, as you can imagine. [#521](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-521)

So margin in LatAm, yes, it is the loss of volume in Mexico in H1, it is a super small part of the explanation of the decrease of the margin because it has only one month effect, June. [#544](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-544)

And the rest is more linked to the fact that as we have a majority of Healthcare, big hospitals where the price index is more or less linked to the inflation of the country and not the reality of inflation of our cost. [#545](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-545)
And when you have a mismatch with -- as we had at the beginning of the year, a lot of increase of the cost of the workforce. [#547](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-547)
And when you see the minimum wage increasing by more than 20% in Colombia, above  10% in Mexico and so on. [#548](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-548)
That means that in reality in our balance of inflation, our cost are increasing much faster than the global inflation of the country. [#549](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-549)
And so you have always a lag effect where you will increase your price less than the increase of your cost. [#550](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-550)

What I expect is regarding the price effect, it will be more balanced in H2 as the opposite, we will have the full effect of loss of volume in Mexico that will put pressure on margin because we will have -- we will lose the operating leverage in Mexico. [#557](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-557)

So that's why all in, what we expect in the second semester in LatAm is to see a decrease of the margin that will be more limited than what we see in '26. [#558](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-558)
And for '27, yes, we still have a part that is not fully hedged, as you have seen in the figures. [#595](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-595)
So of course, we need to be cautious because we cannot anticipate at this level what would be the price for what is not yet hedged. [#597](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-597)
And then contracts, so it's smart to try to have a guidance for '27 that I will not provide today. [#601](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-601)
